subject: Lani Pallister stuns Ledecky + your Monday set
preheader: A new era in swimming's greatest rivalry, plus aerobic builders to start your week.
heroHeading: Good morning swimmers and happy Monday
heroTeaser: Lani Pallister just handed Katie Ledecky a loss at Pan Pacs, and it has everyone asking whether swimming's greatest rivalry is about to flip.
outroLine: That's the week in the water. Happy swimming,

swimSet.title: Today's Swim Set
swimSet.description: Steady, controlled freestyle over longer repeats to build your aerobic engine and teach your body to hold pace when fatigue arrives.

lift.title: Today's Lift
lift.description: A core and stability session focused on rotational power and glute-driven control, dialed in for freestyle and backstroke athletes.

newsItems.title: Pallister Upsets Ledecky. A Rivalry Reborn.
newsItems.body: Lani Pallister scored a significant upset over Katie Ledecky in the women's 800 free at Pan Pacs, adding fresh fuel to the Australia vs. USA rivalry heading into the 2028 Olympic cycle. The win signals that the distance freestyle conversation is no longer a one-country story.

newsItems.title: Nordmann Breaks the Pool Record in the 200 Fly
newsItems.body: Lillie Nordmann time-trialed a pool record 1:55.44 in the 200 butterfly as Northwestern swept Miami (OH) in a dual meet in Evanston. It is the kind of early-season marker that sets a tone for an entire program.

newsItems.title: Cal Men Are Quietly Building Something Special
newsItems.body: David Sammons, ranked number 2 in the Class of 2028, has verbally committed to Cal, giving the program the number 1, 2, 9, and 13-ranked recruits in that class. That is not an accident -- that is a program on a serious run.

newsItems.title: Visualization Works Better When You Feel It
newsItems.body: A new piece on SwimSwam makes the case that effective visualization is not just about picturing your race -- it is about recreating the physical sensation of swimming it. If you are only watching yourself from the outside, you are leaving performance on the table.

athlete.name: Lillie Nordmann
athlete.photoCredit: Photo: Tanis Coralee Leonhardi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
athlete.bio:
Lillie Nordmann is an American competitive swimmer born on August 5, 2002, who specializes in butterfly and freestyle events. She grew up in The Woodlands, Texas, where she trained with club teams and attended The Woodlands High School. She comes from an athletic family, with both parents having competed collegiately in their respective sports. She began attending Stanford University in 2021.

At the 2019 World Junior Swimming Championships in Budapest, Hungary, Nordmann won three gold medals, in the 200 meter butterfly, the 4x200 meter freestyle relay, and the 4x100 meter medley relay. She also won State Championships titles in the 200 yard freestyle and 100 yard butterfly in high school.
